Active mediators identified under each multiplicity method

Source: R/pe_accessors.R
pe_selection.Rd

Summarizes which mediators a pe_mediation() fit identifies as active. When the fit was produced with report_all_methods = TRUE, this reports the active set under each of the three multiplicity methods (Bonferroni for familywise error rate control, Benjamini-Hochberg and Benjamini-Yekutieli for false discovery rate control), so their conservativeness can be compared on the same fit. Otherwise it reports the single method that was used.

Usage

pe_selection(fit)

Arguments

fit

A result from pe_mediation() or one of its workers.

Value

A tidy data.frame of class poemed_tbl (so its p-values print to fixed decimals) with one row per multiplicity method and columns method, n_active (number of active mediators), j_pe (the power enhancement component \(J_m\) under that method's screen), stat_pe and pval_pe (the resulting power-enhanced statistic \(M_{PE}\) and its p-value), and active_mediators (their column names when M has them, otherwise their column positions, comma-separated, or "none"). Because each multiplicity method screens a different active set into \(J_m\), the pval_pe column gives the PE / PE_BH / PE_BY global p-values side by side, as the article's extended data-analysis tables report them.

See also

pe_mediation() (its report_all_methods argument), pe_mediators().

Other mediation tests: pe_lambda_grid(), pe_mediate(), pe_mediation(), pe_mediation_linear(), pe_mediation_logistic(), pe_mediation_poisson(), pe_mediators(), summary.poemed_tbl()

Author

Xiufan Yu and Ken Kelley

Examples

set.seed(113)
d <- simulate_mediation_data(n = 200, p = 60, outcome = "continuous",
                             pattern = "contrasting", c1 = 1)
fit <- pe_mediation(d$X, d$Y, d$M, outcome = "continuous",
                    report_all_methods = TRUE)
pe_selection(fit)
#>  method     n_active j_pe  stat_pe pval_pe  active_mediators
#>  Bonferroni 1        174.1 174.2   < 0.0001 2               
#>  BH         1        174.1 174.2   < 0.0001 2               
#>  BY         1        174.1 174.2   < 0.0001 2
